text: i-am-yuike 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 的人格预设插件，提供猫娘 Yuike 人格及常用 agent 工具。DSH 0.1.7 及以上通过 profile composition 注册预设，0.1.6 则将模板幂等部署到用户目录。预设将 Yuike 设为完整系统提示词，保留 shell、文件操作、计划、压缩、子代理、工作流和网页工具，并关闭 skill 工具链。适合希望用角色化提示词运行 DSH 的用户；旧版部署可通过环境变量调整，无需 API Key。

i-am-yuike adds a Yuike persona preset to DeepSeek Harness web. DSH 0.1.7+ registers it in the profile; 0.1.6 deploys a template. It makes Yuike the system prompt, keeps shell, filesystem, planning, subagent, workflow, and web tools, and disables skills. No API key is needed.
想给 DSH 会话换成可爱猫娘角色的系统提示词。
有没有能在 DeepSeek Harness 里装载角色人格预设的扩展？
让我的 DSH 助手用固定人设、动作括号和口头禅回复。
需要一个保留文件工具和子代理能力的角色预设。
DSH 默认提示内容太多，想让指定人格成为唯一的系统提示词。
旧版 DSH 怎么安装一个不会覆盖我自定义内容的人格预设？
I want a character persona preset for a DeepSeek Harness web session.
How can I keep the main agent tools while changing its system persona?
i-am-yuike 的功能「Yuike 人格预设」：为 agent 注册猫娘角色提示词，设置完整人格提示并使用动作括号、口癖和好感度格式。新建预设会话并选择 yuike 即可使用。
i-am-yuike 的功能「保留 DSH 工具链」：预设组合 shell、文件系统、后台任务、计划、压缩、子代理、工作流和网页工具，并禁用 skill 工具链。会话使用该预设时这些声明的工具随 agent 组合装载。
i-am-yuike 的功能「按 DSH 版本选择部署方式」：profile patch 检测宿主版本，0.1.7 及以上注册声明式预设，旧版则由 node 插件部署模板。插件应用时自动检查并执行对应路径。
i-am-yuike 的功能「旧版预设部署控制」：在 DSH 0.1.6 路径将 template 复制到用户预设目录；目录已存在时默认跳过，也可用环境变量跳过部署或要求重新部署。
i-am-yuike 的功能「可选工具兼容探测」：对时间上下文、日程与子代理列表相关包执行可解析性判定，并按结果禁用不可用的配置行，适配不同 DSH 宿主版本。
i-am-yuike 的功能「计划与会话压缩」：预设组合计划模式与压缩相关组件，包括计划模式指引、压缩命令和工具结果裁剪组件，供会话中按需使用。
i-am-yuike 使用前须知：DSH 0.1.6 路径会把模板部署到 DSH_HOME 下，默认跳过已存在目录；设置 DSH_YUIKE_REDEPLOY=1 会覆盖已有预设。（见 lib/index.js:32-40）
i-am-yuike 使用前须知：预设依赖 DSH 宿主提供配置中引用的工具包；部分时间上下文、日程与子代理行会在解析不到对应包时关闭。

i-am-yuike README · i-am-yuike：A DeepSeek Harness plugin that **ships the 猫娘 Yuike persona preset**. Published on npm as [`i-am-yuike`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/i-am-yuike).

Once installed, pick `yuike` in a new preset session — the catgirl persona takes effect immediately as the sole system prompt: no harness framing, no skill-catalog noise.

i-am-yuike README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add i-am-yuike   # or github:Tkingxiao/I-am-Yuike
dsh web
```

i-am-yuike README · Install：The rows are selected by host version: on **dsh >= 0.1.7** the `preset-yuike` composition row registers the preset directly (nothing is written into `<dshHome>`); on **dsh 0.1.6** the plugin **idempotently deploys** the preset from `template/` to `<dshHome>/.agent-presets/yuike/` (skips if the target already exists — it never overwrites your edited preset). Then open a new preset session and pick `yuike` — the catgirl persona takes effect immediately.

i-am-yuike README · Install：> On a plugin upgrade: on 0.1.7 re-run `dsh plugin --profile web add i-am-yuike@latest` to refresh the declaration row — but a same-id override row in your profile's user patch will keep shadowing the packaged definition (new persona text will not flow in), so delete it to catch up; on 0.1.6 delete `<dshHome>/.agent-presets/yuike` (or set `DSH_YUIKE_REDEPLOY=1`) to pick up the latest changes, since idempotent deploy never overwrites an existing copy on its own.

i-am-yuike README · Usage: thinking mode and persona stability：The persona is anchored by in-session conversation history. If thinking mode is enabled from the very first message, the reasoning pass has no in-character history to condition on and tends to fall back to base assistant behavior — the response explodes on the spot (identity framing, refusals, broken character).

The fix is a two-step warm-up:
section: Usage: thinking mode and persona stability

text:
i-am-yuike README · Usage: thinking mode and persona stability：1. **First conversation: thinking OFF.** Start the session with thinking mode disabled and run your first persona conversation (including 破限向 content) with it off. This writes fully in-character assistant turns into the session history.
2. **Every conversation after: thinking ON.** Re-enable thinking mode from the next exchange onward. The reasoning pass is now conditioned on the in-character history, so the persona holds and thinking works normally.
section: Usage: thinking mode and persona stability

text: i-am-yuike README · Usage: thinking mode and persona stability：Skipping step 1 and opening with thinking on means the persona usually explodes immediately on 破限向 content. Within one session, the warm-up only needs to happen once.
section: Usage: thinking mode and persona stability

text: i-am-yuike README · Persona highlights：The prompt-side and tool-side trims match the sibling project [dsh-novel-solo](https://github.com/Tkingxiao/dsh-novel-solo).

i-am-yuike README · Persona highlights：- **Persona owns the system prompt**: `complete: true` makes the assembled Yuike persona the *only* system-prompt section; `includeRuntimeContext: false` drops the per-round runtime-context snapshots (Current runtime context / DSH file policy / Approval prompts, etc.). The harness identity opener, `@`-path/exit-code rules, and background-job guidance are no longer injected — the catgirl persona leads the prompt cleanly. Tool schemas still inject normally.
- **Zero skill-catalog noise**: disables the `skill-filesystem` / `tool-skill` toolchain. `tool-skill` always injects a `{kind:"skill-catalog",…}` skill catalog message into the session, and there is no way to hide just the catalog while keeping the tool — so the toolchain is disabled instead.
- **Main toolchain kept**: shell (bash/pwsh), filesystem read/write/search, background jobs, schedule reminders (`schedule_create/list/update/delete`), time context, goals, plan & compaction, subagents/workflows, ask-user, todo, web fetch/search, and present all stay available — the same model-visible tool set the 0.2.1 stock `standard` preset exposes. i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：| Host | Mechanism | On plugin upgrade |
|---|---|---|
| **>= 0.1.7** | An `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration row in `cordis.patch.yml`; nothing is written into `<dshHome>` | `dsh plugin --profile web add i-am-yuike@latest` refreshes the row; a same-id row in your profile's user patch keeps overriding this declaration row — drop it to pick up new changes |
| **0.1.6** | The node half idempotently deploys `template/` to `<dshHome>/.agent-presets/yuike/` (never overwrites) | Delete that directory or set `DSH_YUIKE_REDEPLOY=1` |

i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：Both rows live in the same patch and are gated by one shared host-version probe expression (reading the host's own `package.json` version through the loader's `profileContext.installAnchor`) — exactly one activates per host, and the `>= 0.1.7` branch covers 0.2.0 and everything above it. After upgrading the host to 0.1.7, a leftover `.agent-presets/yuike` directory from the old path is simply ignored and can be deleted.

i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：Whether the plugin loads at all is settled earlier, before any of its code runs: since host `0.1.7-rc.1` the profile composition evaluates every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` range in `peerDependencies` against the running release and disables the row when one of them doesn't match, and since `0.2.1-alpha.4` it looks at `engines.dsh` first — once that field is present it decides the verdict alone and `peerDependencies` stops participating (both rules were tested against the host code of `0.2.1-alpha.3` and `0.2.1-rc.2`). So both lists are kept: they name `0.1.6-alpha.1` through `0.2.2-alpha.2` and then end in the open arm `>=0.1.7-alpha.1` with no upper bound, because nothing here is bound to a particular host build: the route is picked by the plugin's own probe at load time, so an unchecked release should still get a working preset rather than lose the plugin to a check that fails closed. The versions named before the open arm are the ones actually compared — `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.2.1-alpha.3` and `0.2.1-rc.2` were run with both plugins installed side by side (the web server boots, `--dump-config` shows both declaration rows and both roster ids, nothin

i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：Three `0.2.2-alpha.2` contract changes this package has caught up with: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents` **no longer exists as a subpath export** — the `list_agents` tool moved into the package's main entry (factory `standard` deleted its own `tool-subagent-list-agents` row in the same release), so `preset-yuike` now probes that subpath and disables the row when it cannot be resolved, which both keeps the tool on 0.2.1 and avoids a duplicate registration on 0.2.2; `tool-subagent`'s `modelSelectionSettings` key was **renamed `modelSelection`** (same semantics, `z.boolean().default(false)`), and since the host's `Config` is a non-strict `z.object` that strips unknown keys without complaining — tested against the installed `zod@4.6.7`, both generations accept `{modelSelectionSettings, modelSelection}` and keep only their own — the row writes both rather than branching; and the persona row's own config (`prefix` / `suffix` / `complete` / `includeRuntimeContext`) is unchanged, as is the strict `{{variable}}` interpolation machinery in `dsh-system-prompt`. What this package could **not** verify from artifacts alone is the *s

i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：Three `0.2.1` contract changes this package has caught up with: the host no longer registers a `{{cwd}}` prompt variable (as of `0.2.1-alpha.2`, so the persona prose uses `{{model}}`); `tool-subagent` dropped `backgroundMode` and `enableRunInBackground` — subagent background execution is unconditional now, so those keys were removed from the rows (they no longer raise an error, they just do nothing); and factory `standard` itself moved on — it added `time-context`, `tool-schedule` and a disabled `plugin-market/tools`, deleted its `tool-ralph` row together with the codex / claude-code provider rows, and reworded the plan-mode guidance. `preset-yuike` now mirrors that generation, ralph included (disabled there too; this package keeps the row switched off as a visible switch).

i-am-yuike README · Host-version adaptation：Why the newer rows are probed instead of just declared: an enabled preset row whose package cannot be resolved is not a skipped row. The Loader logs the failed import and leaves the entry without a fiber, `agent-preset-registry`'s mount audit reads that as `never started`, and its throw fails the **whole** preset — creating a session then reports `agent-preset/invalid`. So `time-context` and `tool-schedule` resolve their own package through `createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)` (the same base the Loader imports these names from, and the same handle the factory `cordis` preset uses) and disable themselves when the probe misses.

i-am-yuike README · Toolchain trims：| State | Rows |
|---|---|
| Kept | tool-bash / tool-pwsh (auto-selected by platform), tool-fs, tool-fs-search, tool-jobs, tool-schedule (probed), time-context (probed), command-goal, tool-goal, plan mode + compaction (with tool-result-pruner), subagent / subagent_fork, list-agents (probed: the `…/list-agents` subpath only exists before 0.2.2, where the main entry does not register the tool), tool-workflow, tool-ask-user, tool-todo, tool-web (fetch on, 60s search timeout), present |
| Disabled | **tool-ralph** (a deliberate preference here — no unattended retry loop under this persona; `standard` dropped the row entirely in 0.2.1), skill-filesystem, tool-skill, tool-plugin-manager, tool-plugin-market (the last three as in the stock standard preset); codex / claude-code providers (a stock host does not install those bundles) |

i-am-yuike README · Toolchain trims：To enable a disabled row: on 0.1.6 delete the `disabled: true` line in the deployed copy; on 0.1.7+ there is no per-row switch — the preset comes wholly from the `preset-yuike` row's `config.plugins`, so remove the `disabled` flag in the packaged definition and reinstall. For the two probed rows, `disabled` is a capability expression rather than a preference: clearing it only helps if the host actually ships that package, and on a host that doesn't the row will take the whole preset down with it.

i-am-yuike README · Files & development：```
cordis.patch.yml             the preset definition itself (0.1.7+ declaration row) + the gated legacy plugin row
lib/                         node/browser halves: mounted on 0.1.6 only, deploys the preset directory
template/                    0.1.6 deploy copy — same source as the patch definition; keep both in sync when editing
```

Develop straight from this repo: `dsh web --patch ./cordis.patch.yml`.

i-am-yuike README · Files & development：Every row id inside the preset carries a `yuike-` prefix: the plugin market scans the patch file line-by-line to decide which entry ids a package owns, and un-prefixed ids such as `persona` / `tool-bash` shared with a sibling plugin (e.g. dsh-novel-solo) are reported as duplicate entries that refuse to install side by side.

i-am-yuike README · Files & development：`{{variable}}` interpolation in the persona text is strict — only variables the host actually registers may be referenced. Today those are `{{model}}` and `{{provider}}`; `{{cwd}}` stopped being registered in host `0.2.1-alpha.2`, so referencing it makes every system-prompt assembly throw.

i-am-yuike README · Environment variables (0.1.6 deploy path only)：| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_HOME` | dsh home directory | `~/.dsh` |
| `DSH_YUIKE_SKIP_DEPLOY` | `1` skips preset deployment | none |
| `DSH_YUIKE_REDEPLOY` | `1` forcibly overwrites an existing preset (use with care) | none |
